components.name: Traffic demo

components.css: .ds-search{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;padding:11px 10px;background:#fffefa;border:1px solid #bfc5ba;border-radius:4px;color:#65705f;font-family:'DM Sans',sans-serif}.ds-search:focus-within{outline:2px solid #a98728;outline-offset:2px}.ds-search input{width:100%;min-width:0;background:none;border:0;outline:none;color:var(--ink,#20272a);font-family:inherit;font-size:12px}.ds-search input::placeholder{color:#747a71}.ds-search kbd{font:10px var(--mono,'IBM Plex Mono',monospace);border:1px solid var(--line,#d9dcd3);border-radius:3px;padding:1px 4px;color:#72796f}

components.name: Map perspective
components.description: Three native pressed-state buttons for Map, Intersection, and Follow. This is not an ARIA tablist.

components.name: Workspace task switch
components.description: Equal-width Cameras, Route, and Driver actions with a 2px active underline and aria-pressed state.
components.css: .ds-task-nav{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr 1fr;border-bottom:1px solid var(--line,#d9dcd3);background:var(--paper,#f5f4ed)}.ds-task-nav button{font-family:'DM Sans',sans-serif;cursor:pointer;transition:background-color 150ms,color 150ms;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:7px;min-height:40px;font-size:12px;color:var(--muted,#626864);border:0;border-bottom:2px solid transparent;background:none;margin-bottom:-1px}.ds-task-nav button:hover{color:var(--ink,#20272a)}.ds-task-nav button[aria-pressed=true]{color:var(--ink,#20272a);border-color:var(--ink,#20272a);font-weight:700}.ds-task-nav button:focus-visible{outline:2px solid #987110;outline-offset:4px}@media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-task-nav button{transition:none}}

components.css: .ds-playback{height:68px;border:1px solid #c6cbbf;background:var(--paper,#f5f4ed);color:var(--ink,#20272a);border-radius:6px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:20px;padding:0 18px;box-shadow:0 3px 20px #0002}.ds-demo-tag{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;min-width:37px;height:30px;font:10px var(--mono,'IBM Plex Mono',monospace);color:#5b4812;background:#f1e3ad;border-radius:3px}.ds-play{font-family:'DM Sans',sans-serif;cursor:pointer;transition:background-color 150ms,color 150ms;border:0;width:34px;height:34px;border-radius:50%;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;background:var(--ink,#20272a);color:var(--paper,#f5f4ed)}.ds-play:hover{background:#465143}.ds-play:focus-visible{outline:2px solid #987110;outline-offset:4px}.ds-timeline{flex:1;min-width:50px;padding-top:10px}.ds-timeline input{display:block;appearance:none;-webkit-appearance:none;height:3px;background:linear-gradient(to right,#536445 0%,#536445 50%,#d4dacd 50%,#d4dacd 100%);border:0;border-radius:3px;width:100%;margin:0;cursor:pointer}.ds-timeline input::-webkit-slider-thumb{appearance:none;width:9px;height:9px;background:#536445;border:0;border-radius:50%}.ds-timeline input::-moz-range-thumb{width:9px;height:9px;background:#536445;border:0;border-radius:50%}.ds-timeline input:focus-visible{outline:2px solid #987110;outline-offset:4px}.ds-times{font:9px var(--mono,'IBM Plex Mono',monospace);color:var(--muted,#626864);display:flex;justify-content:space-between;margin-top:9px}.ds-times span:first-child{color:var(--ink,#20272a)}@media(max-width:760px){.ds-playback{height:65px;padding:0 11px;gap:10px}.ds-play{width:31px;height:31px}.ds-times{font-size:8px}}@media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-play{transition:none}}

narrative.northStar: The New York Street Operations Desk
narrative.overview:
Warm paper, charcoal ink, and taxi yellow frame a dark geographic scene. The interface feels like a compact street operations desk: solid materials, flat rows, thin rules, and clear numbers. Camera imagery and rendered vehicles supply the visual detail.

The map remains the main visual field. Controls use restrained color changes and small functional shadows; the rail provides a consistent reading order for camera selection, route planning, and actual model decisions. The map retains its existing dark controls and mint geographic accents as a separate visual layer.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper controls with a sparse taxi-yellow action accent.
DM Sans for interface language; IBM Plex Mono for speed, time, and numeric metadata.
Flat task rows and measured dividers, with floating instruments above the map.
One Cameras / Route / Driver rail; a modal overlay at narrow widths.
Explicit source and state labels for camera media, simulation playback, and model control.

rules.name: The Paper and Map Rule
rules.body: Use the warm paper palette for workspace controls and preserve the dark geographic layer. Mint belongs to existing map controls and geographic rendering.

rules.name: The Numeric Voice Rule
rules.body: Use IBM Plex Mono for measurements, clocks, counts, and model identifiers; keep explanations, units, and actions in DM Sans.

rules.name: The Flat Rail Rule
rules.body: Keep the rail flat. Use separators and spacing inside it; reserve shadows for surfaces floating over the geographic scene.

dos: Do keep one shared task rail with a visible active underline and text label.
Do use taxi yellow for the next consequential action and charcoal for Stop drive or a selected perspective.
Do retain visible keyboard focus, pressed and expanded states, and readable loading or failure copy.
Do preserve the mobile rail focus trap, inert background, Escape dismissal, and focus restoration.
Do keep camera provenance and simulated-motion labels distinct from real model decisions.
Do account for measured overlays when framing the map and keep mobile captions clear of attribution.
Do disable interface transitions and loading animation for reduced motion while preserving functional simulation controls.
donts: Don't replace flat paper controls with glass, decorative gradients, or repeated dashboard cards.
Don't use mint as a new workspace action color or spread taxi yellow across every surface.
Don't turn the driver panel into a chat transcript; show status, measurements, the latest decision, and optional history.
Don't fabricate a model decision, substitute a replay for a failed model response, or imply that camera images drive this simulation.
Don't style all interface text as monospace or enlarge metadata into competing headlines.
Don't claim every control has a 44px target or that this extraction constitutes a complete accessibility audit.
